decisions.difference: A: approach-algorithm findings (dysuria, frequency, urgency, female, glycosuria, catheter, urinary system disorder, urethral discharge, perineal pain, body aches, prostate tenderness) in a second task  vs  B: same findings in the red-box task

decisions.difference: A: kidney disease and kidney stone criteria written inline (blood/protein, new face/feet swelling, SBP>=140, DBP>=90, oliguria; blood in urine + sudden severe L/R flank/groin pain)  vs  B: (active_condition Kidney disease), (active_condition Kidney stone)
decisions.reason: The red box names 'kidney disease likely' and 'kidney stone likely' for these subsets, and the standard (Will's briefing) says to write a probable rule and reference it with active_condition; A's concern that a pre-existing condition would also fire is recorded for a clinician.

decisions.final_expr: (and Flank pain (or Leukocytes Nitrite) (or vomiting SBP<90 DBP<60 pulse>=100 diabetes male pregnancy postmenopausal))

decisions.difference: A: one rule 'probable acute pyelonephritis' (flank pain + leucocytes/nitrites) for both statements  vs  B: two rules, complicated (with the seven factors) and uncomplicated (flank pain + leucocytes/nitrites)
decisions.final_expr: Diagnose probable complicated pyelonephritis (urinary symptoms); Diagnose probable uncomplicated pyelonephritis (urinary symptoms)
decisions.reason: The page has two 'likely' statements ('complicated pyelonephritis likely' with its factors, 'uncomplicated pyelonephritis likely'), and each 'X likely' becomes a probable rule.

decisions.difference: A: simple UTI = Acute cystitis  vs  B: Lower urinary tract infectious disease
decisions.reason: The page says 'Simple UTI', an infection, not specifically cystitis; B's concept keeps 'urinary tract infection' wording, but SNOMED has no simple-UTI concept so the page does not settle it.

decisions.difference: A: MUS by urethral discharge = Male + Urethral discharge  vs  B: Male + (burning/frequency/urgency or leucocytes/nitrites) + Urethral discharge
decisions.final_expr: (and Male (or Dysuria Frequency Urgency Leukocytes Nitrite) Urethral discharge)
decisions.reason: The Man box sits under the 'Burning/frequency/urgency or leucocytes/nitrites on dipstick' column, so the gate is part of the page's path; a clinician question asks whether discharge alone should suffice.

decisions.difference: A: possible diabetes as two branches (woman / man) each with the gate and (no leucocytes)(no nitrites) glycosuria  vs  B: one and with shared gate and (or Female (and Male no-prostatitis-signs))
decisions.final_expr: (and (or Dysuria Frequency Urgency) (no Leukocytes) (no Nitrite) Glycosuria (or Female (and Male (no Perineal pain) (no Generalized aches and pains) (no Tenderness of prostate))))
decisions.reason: Logically equivalent encodings of 'If glucose, exclude diabetes' / 'If glucose on dipstick, exclude diabetes'; the diff counts only duplicated atoms, so B's base form was kept.

decisions.difference: B only: complicated-pyelonephritis rule conditions (flank pain, leucocytes, nitrite, vomiting, SBP<90, DBP<60, pulse>=100, diabetes, male, pregnancy, postmenopausal)
decisions.reason: Follows from keeping the separate complicated-pyelonephritis rule: 'Flank pain with leucocytes/nitrites on dipstick and any of: vomiting, BP < 90/60, pulse ≥ 100, diabetes, male, pregnant or post menopause'.

notes: Both builds passed. Base is B (follows Will's briefing for active_condition in the priority rule and has one probable rule per 'likely' statement). From A: the split of the non-urgent algorithm's findings into a second task 'Check for urinary infection features'. Remaining questions from both builders merged. Two unsettled decisions: active_condition for kidney disease/stone in the priority rule (A argued pre-existing disease would make the patient Urgent), and the simple-UTI concept (Acute cystitis vs Lower urinary tract infectious disease).
